functions.name: lxw_app_new
functions.description: Create and initialize a new lxw_app object representing the Excel app (docProps/app.xml) part builder within libxlsxwriter. Intended to be paired with lxw_app_free and then populated with heading pairs and part names before writing the XML.
requirements: Must be paired with a subsequent call to lxw_app_free to avoid resource leaks.
Return value must be checked for NULL to handle allocation failures (inferred from allocator naming pattern).
The returned object must be used only with libxlsxwriter app APIs (e.g., lxw_app_add_* and lxw_app_assemble_xml_file).

functions.name: lxw_app_free
functions.description: Release and clean up an lxw_app object created by lxw_app_new, including any associated internal resources.
requirements: app must be a valid pointer previously returned by lxw_app_new (not an arbitrary or stack-allocated object).
Do not use app after calling this function (use-after-free).
Passing NULL is unspecified in this header; callers should avoid passing NULL unless confirmed supported by the implementation (unknown).

functions.name: lxw_app_assemble_xml_file
functions.description: Assemble and write the Excel app XML part (docProps/app.xml) for the workbook using the data stored in the lxw_app object (heading pairs, part names, and properties). Typically called after populating the lxw_app and after associating a writable FILE with it internally by the library.
requirements: self must be a valid lxw_app pointer initialized by lxw_app_new.
self must be in a prepared state with any required fields set by the surrounding libxlsxwriter workflow (e.g., output FILE association is handled by the library; details unknown).
Should be called only once per target output file/part to avoid duplicate or conflicting XML emission (inferred from purpose).

functions.name: lxw_app_add_part_name
functions.description: Add a part name string to the app data that will be written into docProps/app.xml (used to list workbook parts such as worksheets).
requirements: self must be a valid lxw_app pointer created by lxw_app_new.
name must be a valid, null-terminated string pointer; content format requirements are not specified here (unknown).
Ownership/lifetime of name after the call is unspecified; assume the function copies or internally stores data but do not free or modify memory based on undocumented assumptions (unknown).
Should be called before lxw_app_assemble_xml_file so the entry is included in the output.

functions.description: Add a heading pair (key/value) to the app properties that will be written into docProps/app.xml. Heading pairs are used in the app part to describe categories and counts of parts (e.g., "Worksheets", "3").
requirements: self must be a valid lxw_app pointer created by lxw_app_new.
key and value must be valid, null-terminated string pointers; specific encoding or content constraints are not stated here (unknown).
Ownership/lifetime of key and value after the call is unspecified; avoid assumptions about whether the function copies the strings (unknown).
Call before lxw_app_assemble_xml_file to ensure the pair is included in the output.

functions.name: chart_add_series
functions.description: Add a data series to a chart, optionally specifying category and value ranges as Excel-style formulas. Returns a series handle for further configuration.
requirements: chart must be a valid chart pointer.
values is required for a meaningful series; may be NULL if you intend to set via chart_series_set_values().
categories may be NULL to default to 1..n or if you will set via chart_series_set_categories().
categories/values, when non-NULL, must be valid Excel range formulas (e.g., "=Sheet1!$A$1:$A$5") and may be non-contiguous using the "=(range1,range2,...)" form.
Caller should check returned lxw_chart_series* for NULL.

first_row/first_col/last_row/last_col are zero-indexed; last indices must be >= first indices.

functions.name: chart_series_set_values
functions.signature: void chart_series_set_values(lxw_chart_series *series, const char *sheetname, lxw_row_t first_row, lxw_col_t first_col, lxw_row_t last_row, lxw_col_t last_col);
functions.description: Set the series values using sheet name and zero-based row/column bounds instead of a string formula.
requirements: series must be a valid series from chart_add_series().
sheetname must refer to an existing worksheet name.
first_row/first_col/last_row/last_col are zero-indexed; last indices must be >= first indices.

functions.name: chart_series_set_name
functions.description: Set the series name (caption) directly or via a formula (e.g., "=Sheet1!$A$1").
requirements: series must be a valid series from chart_add_series().
If name is a formula it must be a valid single-cell reference formula.

functions.name: chart_series_set_name_range
functions.signature: void chart_series_set_name_range(lxw_chart_series *series, const char *sheetname, lxw_row_t row, lxw_col_t col);
functions.description: Set the series name via a programmatic single-cell reference using sheet name and zero-based row/column.
requirements: series must be valid.
sheetname must refer to an existing worksheet name.
row and col are zero-indexed and must refer to a valid cell.

functions.name: chart_series_set_line
functions.description: Set line/border properties for a series using an lxw_chart_line struct.
requirements: series must be valid.
line may be NULL to use defaults; otherwise fields such as color/width/dash_type must be set as desired (width increments 0.25, transparency 0-100).

functions.name: chart_series_set_fill
functions.description: Set fill properties for a series using an lxw_chart_fill struct.
requirements: series must be valid.
fill may be NULL to use defaults; otherwise transparency must be 0-100.

functions.name: chart_series_set_invert_if_negative
functions.description: Invert the series fill color for negative values (mainly for column/bar charts).
requirements: series must be valid.
Applies primarily to Bar/Column charts; has no effect on chart types without fills.

functions.name: chart_series_set_pattern
functions.description: Set pattern fill properties for a series using an lxw_chart_pattern struct.
requirements: series must be valid.
pattern must point to a struct with a valid type from lxw_chart_pattern_type.

functions.name: chart_series_set_marker_type
functions.description: Set the marker type for a series (applicable to Line, Scatter, Radar variants).
requirements: series must be valid.
type must be a valid lxw_chart_marker_type.
LXW_CHART_MARKER_NONE disables markers; LXW_CHART_MARKER_AUTOMATIC enables default markers and prevents setting size/line/fill.

functions.name: chart_series_set_marker_size
functions.description: Set the size of the data markers for a series.
requirements: series must be valid.
A marker type should be set/enabled for size to take effect.
size must be within Excel’s acceptable range (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: chart_series_set_marker_line
functions.description: Set line/border properties for series markers.
requirements: series must be valid.
Markers should be enabled and not LXW_CHART_MARKER_AUTOMATIC.
line may be NULL to use defaults; transparency 0-100, width in 0.25 increments.

functions.name: chart_series_set_marker_fill
functions.description: Set fill properties for series markers.
requirements: series must be valid.
Markers should be enabled and not LXW_CHART_MARKER_AUTOMATIC.
fill may be NULL; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_series_set_marker_pattern
functions.description: Set pattern fill for series markers.
requirements: series must be valid.
Markers should be enabled and not LXW_CHART_MARKER_AUTOMATIC.
pattern type must be a valid lxw_chart_pattern_type.

functions.name: chart_series_set_points
functions.description: Apply formatting to individual points in a series (e.g., Pie/Doughnut segments) using a NULL-terminated array of lxw_chart_point pointers.
requirements: series must be valid.
points must be a NULL-terminated array; each non-NULL entry points to an lxw_chart_point with optional line/fill/pattern.
Caller must check the returned lxw_error for success.

functions.name: chart_series_set_smooth
functions.description: Enable/disable smoothing for Line/Scatter series.
requirements: series must be valid.
smooth must be 0 or 1.
Only applicable to Line and Scatter chart types.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels
functions.description: Turn on data labels for a series (values shown by default).
requirements: series must be valid.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_options
functions.signature: void chart_series_set_labels_options(lxw_chart_series *series, uint8_t show_name, uint8_t show_category, uint8_t show_value);
functions.description: Control which items (series name, category, value) are shown in data labels.
requirements: series must be valid.
show_name/show_category/show_value are 0/1 flags.
chart_series_set_labels() should be enabled to display labels.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_custom
functions.description: Set custom properties or hide specific data labels using a NULL-terminated array of lxw_chart_data_label pointers.
requirements: series must be valid and labels enabled if you want them displayed.
data_labels must be a NULL-terminated array; entries may be NULL to accept defaults; each non-NULL may specify value (string or formula) and optional font/line/fill/pattern.
Caller must check the returned lxw_error for success.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_separator
functions.description: Set the separator used between multiple label fields (comma, semicolon, period, newline, space).
requirements: series must be valid.
separator must be one of lxw_chart_label_separator values.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_position
functions.description: Set the position of data labels relative to points. Valid positions vary by chart type.
requirements: series must be valid.
position must be one of lxw_chart_label_position values.
Some positions are only applicable to certain chart types as per documentation.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_leader_line
functions.description: Enable leader lines for data labels (mainly for Pie/Doughnut). Visible only when labels are repositioned/overlapped in Excel.
requirements: series must be valid.
Primarily applicable to Pie/Doughnut charts.
Labels should be enabled.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_legend
functions.description: Show the legend key alongside data labels for a series.
requirements: series must be valid.
Labels should be enabled to see effect.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_percentage
functions.description: Show data labels as percentages (mainly for Pie charts).
requirements: series must be valid.
Typically used with Pie/Doughnut charts.
Consider turning off other label parts if only percentage is desired.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_num_format
functions.description: Set the number format string for data labels (similar to cell num_format).
requirements: series must be valid.
num_format must be a valid Excel number format string.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_font
functions.description: Set font properties for data labels in a series.
requirements: series must be valid.
font may be NULL; if setting bold off explicitly use LXW_EXPLICIT_FALSE where required (note applies to title fonts; same struct).

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_line
functions.description: Set line/border properties for the label boxes.
requirements: series must be valid.
line may be NULL; transparency 0-100, width increments 0.25.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_fill
functions.description: Set fill properties for the label boxes.
requirements: series must be valid.
fill may be NULL; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_series_set_labels_pattern
functions.description: Set pattern fill for the label boxes.
requirements: series must be valid.
pattern type must be valid lxw_chart_pattern_type.

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline
functions.description: Enable a trendline for a series with a given type; value is the order (POLY) or period (AVERAGE), ignored for other types.
requirements: series must be valid.
type must be one of lxw_chart_trendline_type.
For POLY and AVERAGE types, value must be >= 2; value is ignored for other types.

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline_forecast
functions.description: Set forward and backward forecast periods for the trendline.
requirements: series must be valid and have a trendline set.
Not available for Moving Average trendlines (Excel limitation).

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline_equation
functions.description: Display the trendline equation on the chart.
requirements: series must be valid and have a trendline set.
Not available for Moving Average trendlines.

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline_r_squared
functions.description: Display the R-squared value for the trendline on the chart.
requirements: series must be valid and have a trendline set.
Not available for Moving Average trendlines.

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline_intercept
functions.description: Set a fixed Y-intercept for the trendline (where X=0).
requirements: series must be valid and have a trendline set.
Available only for Exponential, Linear, and Polynomial trendline types.

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline_name
functions.description: Set the trendline name displayed in the legend.
requirements: series must be valid and have a trendline set.
name is a string; can be any caption suitable for legend.

functions.name: chart_series_set_trendline_line
functions.description: Set the line properties for a series trendline.
requirements: series must be valid and have a trendline set.
line may be NULL; width increments 0.25; transparency 0-100; dash_type valid.

functions.name: chart_series_get_error_bars
functions.description: Retrieve a pointer to the X or Y error bars for a series, for configuration via the error bar setter functions.
requirements: series must be valid.
axis_type must be LXW_CHART_ERROR_BAR_AXIS_X or LXW_CHART_ERROR_BAR_AXIS_Y.
May return NULL if not found; caller must check for NULL.

functions.name: chart_series_set_error_bars
functions.description: Configure error bars: type and associated value (ignored for Standard Error).
requirements: error_bars must be a valid pointer (e.g., series->x_error_bars or ->y_error_bars, or from chart_series_get_error_bars()).
type must be one of lxw_chart_error_bar_type.
For all types except STD_ERROR, value must be provided and meaningful.

functions.name: chart_series_set_error_bars_direction
functions.description: Set error bar direction (both/plus/minus).
requirements: error_bars must be valid.
direction must be one of lxw_chart_error_bar_direction.

functions.name: chart_series_set_error_bars_endcap
functions.description: Set error bar end cap style (flat or none).
requirements: error_bars must be valid.
endcap must be one of lxw_chart_error_bar_cap.

functions.name: chart_series_set_error_bars_line
functions.description: Set line properties for error bars.
requirements: error_bars must be valid.
line may be NULL; width increments 0.25; transparency 0-100; dash_type valid.

functions.name: chart_axis_get
functions.description: Get a pointer to the chart’s X or Y axis for further configuration.
requirements: chart must be valid.
axis_type must be LXW_CHART_AXIS_TYPE_X or LXW_CHART_AXIS_TYPE_Y.
May return NULL if the axis isn’t found; caller must check.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_name
functions.description: Set the axis title/caption directly or by formula (e.g., "=Sheet1!$A$1").
requirements: axis must be a valid axis pointer (e.g., chart->x_axis or chart->y_axis).
If name is a formula it must reference a single cell.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_name_range
functions.signature: void chart_axis_set_name_range(lxw_chart_axis *axis, const char *sheetname, lxw_row_t row, lxw_col_t col);
functions.description: Set the axis title via a programmatic single-cell reference.
requirements: axis must be valid.
sheetname must exist.
row/col are zero-based indices pointing to a valid cell.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_name_layout
functions.description: Manually position the axis title using relative layout units.
requirements: axis must be valid.
layout->x,y in (0.0, 1.0]; width/height in (0.0, 1.0] when used.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_name_font
functions.description: Set font properties for the axis title.
requirements: axis must be valid.
font may be NULL; rotation allowed values include -90..90 and 270, 271, 360; color valid; to explicitly disable bold use LXW_EXPLICIT_FALSE.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_num_font
functions.description: Set font properties for the axis numbers.
requirements: axis must be valid.
font may be NULL; rotation valid range as per lxw_chart_font.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_num_format
functions.description: Set number format for axis tick labels.
requirements: axis must be valid.
num_format must be a valid Excel number format string.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_line
functions.description: Set axis line/border properties or hide it via .none.
requirements: axis must be valid.
line may be NULL; transparency 0-100; width increments 0.25; dash_type valid.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_fill
functions.description: Set fill properties for the axis area.
requirements: axis must be valid.
fill may be NULL; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_pattern
functions.description: Set pattern fill for the axis area.
requirements: axis must be valid.
pattern must have a valid lxw_chart_pattern_type.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_reverse
functions.description: Reverse the order of axis categories/values.
requirements: axis must be valid.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_crossing
functions.description: Set the point (category index or value) where the axis crosses the opposite axis.
requirements: axis must be valid.
value should be within the axis’ data range for meaningful results.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_crossing_max
functions.description: Set the opposite axis to cross at this axis’ maximum.
requirements: axis must be valid.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_crossing_min
functions.description: Set the opposite axis to cross at this axis’ minimum.
requirements: axis must be valid.

functions.name: chart_axis_off
functions.description: Hide/turn off an axis (including line and tick marks).
requirements: axis must be valid.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_position
functions.description: For category axes, position the axis on tick marks or between tick marks.
requirements: axis must be a category axis.
position must be LXW_CHART_AXIS_POSITION_ON_TICK or LXW_CHART_AXIS_POSITION_BETWEEN.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_label_position
functions.description: Position axis labels (next to, high, low, or none).
requirements: axis must be valid.
position must be one of lxw_chart_axis_label_position values.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_label_align
functions.description: Set alignment for category axis labels (center/left/right).
requirements: axis must be a category axis.
align must be one of lxw_chart_axis_label_alignment values.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_min
functions.description: Set minimum for axis range (value/date axes).
requirements: axis must be a value or date axis.
min must be <= max if max is set.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_max
functions.description: Set maximum for axis range (value/date axes).
requirements: axis must be a value or date axis.
max must be >= min if min is set.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_log_base
functions.description: Set logarithmic base for a value axis.
requirements: axis must be a value axis.
log_base must be in the range 2..1000.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_major_tick_mark
functions.description: Set major tick mark type for an axis.
requirements: axis must be valid.
type must be one of lxw_chart_tick_mark values.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_minor_tick_mark
functions.description: Set minor tick mark type for an axis.
requirements: axis must be valid.
type must be one of lxw_chart_tick_mark values.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_interval_unit
functions.description: Set the interval between category/date values (labels).
requirements: Axis must be a category or date axis.
unit must be a positive integer (default is 1).

functions.name: chart_axis_set_interval_tick
functions.description: Set the interval between category tick marks.
requirements: Axis must be a category or date axis.
unit must be a positive integer (default is 1).

functions.name: chart_axis_set_major_unit
functions.description: Set increment of major units for value/date axes.
requirements: Axis must be a value or date axis.
unit must be > 0 for meaningful effect.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_minor_unit
functions.description: Set increment of minor units for value/date axes.
requirements: Axis must be a value or date axis.
unit must be > 0 for meaningful effect.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_display_units
functions.description: Set display units for a value axis (hundreds, thousands, millions, etc.).
requirements: Axis must be a value axis.
units must be one of lxw_chart_axis_display_unit values.

functions.name: chart_axis_set_display_units_visible
functions.description: Toggle visibility of display units labels on a value axis.
requirements: Axis must be a value axis.
visible is 0/1.
Calling chart_axis_set_display_units() implies visible on; this toggles it.

functions.name: chart_axis_major_gridlines_set_visible
functions.description: Turn major gridlines on/off for an axis.
requirements: axis must be valid.
visible is 0/1.

functions.name: chart_axis_minor_gridlines_set_visible
functions.description: Turn minor gridlines on/off for an axis.
requirements: axis must be valid.
visible is 0/1.

functions.name: chart_axis_major_gridlines_set_line
functions.description: Set line properties for major gridlines.
requirements: axis must be valid.
line may be NULL; width increments 0.25; dash_type valid; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_axis_minor_gridlines_set_line
functions.description: Set line properties for minor gridlines.
requirements: axis must be valid.
line may be NULL; width increments 0.25; dash_type valid; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_title_set_name
functions.description: Set the chart title text directly or via a formula (e.g., "=Sheet1!$A$1").
requirements: chart must be valid.
If name is a formula it must be a valid single-cell reference.
Default Excel behavior is no title unless set or auto-added for single-series with name.

functions.name: chart_title_set_name_range
functions.signature: void chart_title_set_name_range(lxw_chart *chart, const char *sheetname, lxw_row_t row, lxw_col_t col);
functions.description: Set the chart title from a specific cell using sheet name and zero-based row/column.
requirements: chart must be valid.
sheetname must exist.
row/col must point to a valid cell.

functions.name: chart_title_set_name_font
functions.description: Set font properties for the chart title.
requirements: chart must be valid.
font may be NULL; for explicitly turning bold off use LXW_EXPLICIT_FALSE; rotation allowed values as documented.

functions.name: chart_title_off
functions.description: Turn off the automatic chart title that Excel may add for single-series charts with a series name.
requirements: chart must be valid.

functions.name: chart_title_set_layout
functions.description: Manually position the chart title using relative layout units.
requirements: chart must be valid.
layout->x,y in (0.0,1.0]; width/height in (0.0,1.0] if used.

functions.name: chart_title_set_overlay
functions.description: Allow the chart title to overlay the chart plot area when manual layout is set.
requirements: chart must be valid.
overlay is 0/1.
Typically used with chart_title_set_layout().

functions.name: chart_legend_set_position
functions.description: Set legend position or hide it using lxw_chart_legend_position values.
requirements: chart must be valid.
position must be a valid lxw_chart_legend_position value.

functions.name: chart_legend_set_layout
functions.description: Manually position the legend using relative layout units.
requirements: chart must be valid.
layout->x,y in (0.0,1.0]; width/height in (0.0,1.0] if used.

functions.name: chart_legend_set_font
functions.description: Set font properties for legend text.
requirements: chart must be valid.
font may be NULL; rotation allowed values as per lxw_chart_font.

functions.name: chart_legend_delete_series
functions.description: Remove/hide one or more zero-indexed series names from the legend; series still display in the chart. The list must be terminated by -1.
requirements: chart must be valid.
delete_series must be an array of zero-based series indices terminated by -1.
Caller must check lxw_error return value.

functions.name: chart_chartarea_set_line
functions.description: Set line/border properties for the chartarea (the background behind the chart).
requirements: chart must be valid.
line may be NULL; .none can hide; width increments 0.25; transparency 0-100; dash_type valid.

functions.name: chart_chartarea_set_fill
functions.description: Set fill for the chartarea.
requirements: chart must be valid.
fill may be NULL; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_chartarea_set_pattern
functions.description: Set pattern fill for the chartarea.
requirements: chart must be valid.
pattern->type must be a valid lxw_chart_pattern_type.

functions.name: chart_plotarea_set_line
functions.description: Set line/border properties for the plotarea (area bounded by axes).
requirements: chart must be valid.
line may be NULL; width increments 0.25; transparency 0-100; dash_type valid.

functions.name: chart_plotarea_set_fill
functions.description: Set fill for the plotarea.
requirements: chart must be valid.
fill may be NULL; transparency 0-100.

functions.name: chart_plotarea_set_pattern
functions.description: Set pattern fill for the plotarea.
requirements: chart must be valid.
pattern->type must be a valid lxw_chart_pattern_type.

functions.name: chart_plotarea_set_layout
functions.description: Manually set plotarea layout using relative units (x,y,width,height).
requirements: chart must be valid.
layout->x,y,width,height in (0.0,1.0].

functions.name: chart_set_style
functions.description: Apply one of Excel’s built-in chart styles (1-48).
requirements: chart must be valid.
style_id must be in 1..48 (Excel 2007 styles; default is 2).

functions.name: chart_set_table
functions.description: Enable a data table below the horizontal axis showing the plotted data (Bar/Column/Line/Area only).
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only supported for Bar, Column, Line, and Area charts.

functions.name: chart_set_table_grid
functions.signature: void chart_set_table_grid(lxw_chart *chart, uint8_t horizontal, uint8_t vertical, uint8_t outline, uint8_t legend_keys);
functions.description: Configure data table grid options (horizontal, vertical, outline lines, and legend keys).
requirements: chart must be valid and data table should be enabled (chart_set_table()).
Each flag is 0/1.
Only available for Bar, Column, Line, and Area charts.

functions.name: chart_set_table_font
functions.description: Set the font for the data table.
requirements: chart must be valid.
font may be NULL; typical font field constraints apply.

functions.name: chart_set_up_down_bars
functions.description: Enable Up-Down bars for Line charts to show differences between first and last series.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only available for Line charts.

functions.name: chart_set_up_down_bars_format
functions.signature: void chart_set_up_down_bars_format(lxw_chart *chart, lxw_chart_line *up_bar_line, lxw_chart_fill *up_bar_fill, lxw_chart_line *down_bar_line, lxw_chart_fill *down_bar_fill);
functions.description: Enable and format Up-Down bars for Line charts, specifying line/fill for up and down bars.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only available for Line charts.
Any of the line/fill pointers may be NULL to use defaults; color/transparency/width constraints apply.

functions.name: chart_set_drop_lines
functions.description: Enable and optionally format Drop Lines (category value projection) for Line/Area charts.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only available for Line and Area charts.
line may be NULL or formatted; dash_type/width/transparency constraints apply.

functions.name: chart_set_high_low_lines
functions.description: Enable and optionally format High-Low Lines for Line charts.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only available for Line charts.
line may be NULL or formatted; dash_type/width/transparency constraints apply.

functions.name: chart_set_series_overlap
functions.description: Set overlap between series in Bar/Column charts.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only available for Bar/Column charts.
overlap must be in the range -100 to 100 (per parameter description).

functions.name: chart_set_series_gap
functions.description: Set the gap width between series categories in Bar/Column charts.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only available for Bar/Column charts.
gap must be in the range 0..500 (default 150).

functions.name: chart_show_blanks_as
functions.description: Control how blank cells are displayed in the chart (gaps, zero, or connected for line charts).
requirements: chart must be valid.
option must be one of lxw_chart_blank values.
CONNECTED is only for charts with lines.

functions.name: chart_show_hidden_data
functions.description: Display data from hidden rows/columns in the chart.
requirements: chart must be valid.

functions.name: chart_set_rotation
functions.description: Set rotation angle of first slice/point for Pie/Doughnut charts (effectively rotates chart).
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only applicable to Pie/Doughnut charts.
rotation must be in 0..360.

functions.name: chart_set_hole_size
functions.description: Set the Doughnut hole size as a percentage.
requirements: chart must be valid.
Only applicable to Doughnut charts.
size must be in 10..90.

functions.name: lxw_chart_add_data_cache
functions.signature: lxw_error lxw_chart_add_data_cache(lxw_series_range *range, uint8_t *data, uint16_t rows, uint8_t cols, uint8_t col);
functions.description: Internal/helper API to add cached data points to a series range (for embedded string/number caches).
requirements: range must be a valid series range.
data must point to an array with at least rows*cols entries (layout and encoding are library-internal).
rows, cols, and col must be within the expected bounds; col selects the column in data to use.
Caller must check lxw_error return value.

functions.name: chartsheet_set_chart
functions.description: Insert an existing chart object into the specified chartsheet so it becomes the sole content of that chartsheet. Typically used after creating and configuring a chart via workbook_add_chart() and chart APIs.
requirements: chartsheet must be a valid, initialized lxw_chartsheet pointer created via workbook_add_chartsheet().
chart must be a valid lxw_chart created via workbook_add_chart() and configured as needed before insertion.
A chart may be inserted only once into either a single chartsheet or a worksheet; the same chart object must not be added to multiple sheets.
Function returns an lxw_error; callers should check the return value for failure.

functions.name: chartsheet_set_chart_opt
functions.description: Variant of chartsheet_set_chart that accepts chart options. Comment indicates options (such as scale) are not currently useful for chartsheets; primarily present for API symmetry.
requirements: chartsheet must be a valid, initialized lxw_chartsheet pointer.
chart must be a valid lxw_chart; as with chartsheet_set_chart, a chart may be inserted only once into a single sheet.
user_options usage for chartsheets is currently not required/meaningful per header comment; passing NULL is expected to behave like chartsheet_set_chart.
Function returns an lxw_error; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: chartsheet_activate
functions.description: Make the given chartsheet the initially visible (active) sheet when the workbook is opened. Only one sheet can be active at a time.
requirements: chartsheet must be a valid, initialized lxw_chartsheet pointer.
Only one sheet can be active; subsequent calls override previous activation.
A hidden chartsheet cannot be activated.

functions.name: chartsheet_select
functions.description: Mark the chartsheet’s tab as selected (highlighted). Multiple sheets can be selected for grouped operations such as printing.

Passing both password == NULL and options == NULL has no effect on chartsheets.

functions.name: worksheet_split_panes_opt

functions.name: lxw_new_attribute_str
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new xml_attribute containing a key/value pair where the value is provided as a C string. On allocation or conversion failure this function may return NULL; callers must handle a NULL return.

functions.name: lxw_new_attribute_dbl

requirements: key must point to a valid, nul-terminated string.
The returned pointer refers to heap-allocated memory; the caller must eventually free it (for example via the LXW_FREE_ATTRIBUTES list-cleanup macro or free()).

tag must be a valid, nul-terminated string naming the element.
attributes may be NULL or a properly initialized xml_attribute_list (STAILQ) of xml_attribute items.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: generic string buffers consumed by many FUZZ_PARAM_STR and filenames.
# Strategy:
# - Generate short, valid, NULL-terminated friendly ASCII-heavy strings that are
#   acceptable in multiple contexts (XML text, sheet names, URLs, captions, keys, etc.).
# - Occasionally generate strings tailored to specific APIs seen in stubs:
#   * Excel A1 formulas like =Sheet1!$A$1
#   * Worksheet/chartsheet-safe names (<=31 chars, without invalid characters)
#   * URL-like prefixes
#   * Printable text with a mix of punctuation
#   * Short numeric strings
#   * XML-safe fragments
# - For FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, the harness will create a temp path; our buffer is the
#   file content source for those calls that write files before use (e.g., BMP builder).
#   Therefore we keep bytes modest and generic.
# - We pack multiple candidate strings separated by newlines so the fuzzer can slice
#   or reuse segments; common fuzzer harnesses pick tokens by splitting or slicing.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SAFE_ASCII = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127))
PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '


def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Bias towards letters/digits to increase validity across APIs
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ' _-.,:+/()#%'
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _sheet_safe_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # <=31 chars, exclude []:*?/\ and avoid leading/trailing apostrophe
    raw = _rand_printable(r, 3, 31)
    bad = set('[]:*?/\\')
    name = ''.join(ch for ch in raw if ch not in bad)
    if not name:
        name = 'Sheet'
    if name[0] == "'":
        name = 'S' + name
    if name[-1] == "'":
        name = name + 'S'
    return name[:31]


def _formula_single_cell(r: random.Random) -> str:
    col = chr(ord('A') + r.randrange(26))
    row = r.randrange(1, 100)
    return f"=Sheet1!${col}${row}"


def _url_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    schemes = ['http://', 'https://', 'mailto:', 'ftp://']
    path = _rand_printable(r, 5, 64)
    # Clean path to printable without spaces for URLs
    path = ''.join(ch if ch not in '\n\r\t ' else '_' for ch in path)
    return schemes[r.randrange(len(schemes))] + path


def _xml_safe_tag(r: random.Random) -> str:
    first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + '_:')
    rest_len = r.randint(0, 20)
    rest_alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_.-:'
    return first + ''.join(r.choice(rest_alphabet) for _ in range(rest_len))


def _numeric_str(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes integer, sometimes float
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return str(r.randint(-100000, 100000))
    else:
        return f"{r.uniform(-1e6, 1e6):.6f}"


def _caption(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    s = _rand_printable(r, 1, max_len)
    # Make it friendly text
    return s.strip() or 'x'


def _xml_data(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include escapable characters sometimes
    base = _rand_printable(r, 1, 40)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        inserts = ['&', '<', '>', '"']
        pos = r.randrange(len(base))
        base = base[:pos] + r.choice(inserts) + base[pos:]
    return base


def _author(r: random.Random) -> str:
    first = r.choice(['Ava', 'Bob', 'Chen', 'Dee', 'Eli', 'Fran', 'Gus', 'Hana'])
    last = r.choice(['Smith', 'Jones', 'Lee', 'Patel', 'Kim', 'Lopez', 'Singh'])
    return f"{first} {last}"


def _title_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    nouns = ['Report', 'Summary', 'Analysis', 'Dashboard', 'Metrics', 'Trends', 'Overview']
    years = str(2000 + r.randrange(40))
    return f"{r.choice(nouns)} {years}"


def _make_token_set(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens: List[str] = []
    # Core document props
    tokens.append(_title_like(r))
    tokens.append(_author(r))
    tokens.append('Acme Corp')
    tokens.append('Finance')
    tokens.append('status: draft')
    tokens.append('keywords: quarterly, revenue')
    tokens.append('http://example.com/base')
    # Worksheet/chartsheet names
    for _ in range(3):
        tokens.append(_sheet_safe_name(r))
    # Formulas
    for _ in range(3):
        tokens.append(_formula_single_cell(r))
    # URLs
    for _ in range(3):
        tokens.append(_url_like(r))
    # Captions and labels
    tokens.append(_caption(r, 16))
    tokens.append(_caption(r, 32))
    tokens.append(_caption(r, 48))
    # XML tags/data
    for _ in range(3):
        tokens.append(_xml_safe_tag(r))
    for _ in range(3):
        tokens.append(_xml_data(r))
    # Numeric strings
    for _ in range(3):
        tokens.append(_numeric_str(r))
    # General printable strings suitable for many setters
    for _ in range(6):
        tokens.append(_rand_printable(r, 3, 24))
    # Short passwords
    tokens.append(_rand_printable(r, 0, 12))
    # Ensure some non-empty ASCII lines for APIs that require non-empty
    tokens.append('x')
    tokens.append('y')
    return tokens


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    tokens = _make_token_set(r)

    # Shuffle to diversify first-consumed entries
    r.shuffle(tokens)

    # Assemble as newline-separated UTF-8 bytes; many harnesses consume sequential FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    buf = ('\n'.join(tokens)).encode('utf-8')

    # Ensure size cap
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return buf

#
# Strategy:
# - Include several minimal valid BMP images (1x1, 2x2) since many stubs insert/embed
#   BMPs from filenames. BMP is simple and accepted by the library.
# - Include small well-formed XML fragments because many stubs write/read XML files
#   (having existing content can exercise truncate/overwrite paths or mixed IO modes).
# - Include empty and random small buffers to exercise edge cases where stubs open
#   files and write into them.
# - Keep outputs small (< 1 KiB) and deterministic per seed with variation across calls.


def _bmp_24bpp(width: int, height: int, rgb: List[tuple]) -> bytes:
    # Create a minimal BMP (BITMAPFILEHEADER + BITMAPINFOHEADER + pixel data)
    # 24bpp, BI_RGB, bottom-up. Row size must be padded to multiple of 4 bytes.
    # rgb: list of (R,G,B) rows in bottom-up order sized width*height if provided;
    # if shorter, repeat pattern.
    row_stride = (width * 3 + 3) & ~3
    pixel_data = bytearray()
    idx = 0
    for y in range(height):
        row = bytearray()
        for x in range(width):
            r, g, b = rgb[idx % len(rgb)]
            idx += 1
            # BMP stores B,G,R
            row += bytes((b & 0xFF, g & 0xFF, r & 0xFF))
        # pad
        while len(row) < row_stride:
            row.append(0)
        pixel_data += row
    biSizeImage = len(pixel_data)
    bfOffBits = 14 + 40
    bfSize = bfOffBits + biSizeImage
    # BITMAPFILEHEADER
    bfType = b"BM"
    bfReserved1 = 0
    bfReserved2 = 0
    file_header = struct.pack('<2sIHHI', bfType, bfSize, bfReserved1, bfReserved2, bfOffBits)
    # BITMAPINFOHEADER
    biSize = 40
    biWidth = width
    biHeight = height
    biPlanes = 1
    biBitCount = 24
    biCompression = 0  # BI_RGB
    biXPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biYPelsPerMeter = 2835
    biClrUsed = 0
    biClrImportant = 0
    info_header = struct.pack('<IIIHHIIIIII', biSize, biWidth, biHeight, biPlanes, biBitCount,
                              biCompression, biSizeImage, biXPelsPerMeter, biYPelsPerMeter,
                              biClrUsed, biClrImportant)
    return file_header + info_header + pixel_data


def _xml_samples(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Small, well-formed XML snippets relevant to libxlsxwriter parts
    tags = [
        ("Types", "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"),
        ("Relationships", "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships"),
        ("sst", "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main"),
        ("styleSheet", "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main"),
        ("Properties", "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/extended-properties"),
    ]
    tag, ns = rnd.choice(tags)
    content = [
        b"<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\" standalone=\"yes\"?>\n",
        f"<{tag} xmlns=\"{ns}\">".encode(),
    ]
    # Add a couple of simple child elements safely
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 3)):
        name = rnd.choice(["Default", "Override", "si", "font", "fmt", "lp", "HeadingPairs", "PartNames"]) \
               + ("" if rnd.random() < 0.6 else str(rnd.randint(1, 9)))
        attrs = []
        if name == "Default":
            attrs.append(("Extension", "xml"))
            attrs.append(("ContentType", "application/xml"))
        elif name == "Override":
            attrs.append(("PartName", "/docProps/app.xml"))
            attrs.append(("ContentType", "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.extended-properties+xml"))
        elif name == "si":
            # Shared string item with simple text
            content.append(b"<si><t>hello</t></si>")
            continue
        # build start-empty tag
        if attrs:
            att = b" ".join(f"{k}=\"{v}\"".encode() for k, v in attrs)
            content.append(b"<" + name.encode() + b" " + att + b"/>")
        else:
            content.append(b"<" + name.encode() + b"/>")
    content.append(f"</{tag}>".encode())
    return b"\n".join(content)[:1024]


def _random_ascii(rnd: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Visible ASCII data that could serve as generic file content
    alphabet = [c for c in range(32, 127)]
    return bytes(rnd.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    choice = rnd.random()
    # Weights tuned toward BMP since many stubs require valid images
    if choice < 0.45:
        # 1x1 or 2x2 BMP with simple colors
        w = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.7 else 2
        h = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.7 else 2
        palette = [
            (255, 0, 0),   # red
            (0, 255, 0),   # green
            (0, 0, 255),   # blue
            (255, 255, 255),  # white
            (0, 0, 0),     # black
        ]
        colors = [rnd.choice(palette) for _ in range(max(1, w * h))]
        return _bmp_24bpp(w, h, colors)
    elif choice < 0.75:
        # XML content likely to be accepted/overwritten by writer stubs
        return _xml_samples(rnd)
    elif choice < 0.90:
        # Empty file (some stubs open wb+ and will write); valid edge case
        return b""
    else:
        # Small random ASCII data (for fopen/read/write paths)
        size = rnd.randint(1, 256)
        return _random_ascii(rnd, size)

import random
import string

# Generator for valid Excel A1 single-cell formulas like "=Sheet1!$A$1".
# Fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR as either literal captions or formulas,
# and also construct their own formulas. We provide strings that are often
# valid sheet references, axis/series titles, or plausible defined names to
# explore both branches. The buffer will contain multiple newline-separated
# entries so the fuzzer can draw from them.

MAX_BUF = 4096

LETTERS = string.ascii_uppercase

def excel_col(n: int) -> str:
    # 1-based to letters; limit to 1-3 letters up to XFD (16384)
    n = max(1, min(n, 16384))
    s = []
    while n:
        n, r = divmod(n - 1, 26)
        s.append(chr(ord('A') + r))
    return ''.join(reversed(s))

def make_sheet_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a valid sheet name without invalid chars: : \ / ? * [ ]
    base_choices = [
        "Sheet1", "Data", "Summary", "Charts", "ðSheet", "Budget_2025",
        "Sales Q1", "S" + str(rng.randint(2, 99)),
    ]
    name = rng.choice(base_choices)
    # Occasionally add quotes if spaces/specials present
    if any(ch in name for ch in [' ',"'","-","ð"]):
        # If contains single quote, escape by doubling inside quoted name
        inner = name.replace("'", "''")
        return f"'{inner}'"
    return name

def make_a1_single_cell(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    row = rng.randint(1, 1048576)  # Excel max rows
    col = rng.randint(1, 16384)    # Excel max cols
    col_str = excel_col(col)
    return f"${col_str}${row}"

def make_single_cell_formula(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sheet = make_sheet_name(rng)
    ref = make_a1_single_cell(rng)
    return f"={sheet}!{ref}"

def make_caption(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    # A readable short caption suitable for titles/axis names
    words = [
        "Revenue", "Expenses", "Profit", "Growth", "Series", "Axis",
        "Title", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4", "FY", "2025", "Units",
    ]
    s = rng.choice(words)
    # Occasionally compose multi-word captions
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s = f"{rng.choice(words)} {rng.choice(words)}"
    # Add a number suffix sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        s += f" {rng.randint(1, 100)}"
    # Ensure length bound
    return s[:max_len]

def make_defined_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid-ish defined name: starts with letter or underscore, then letters/digits/underscore
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest_len = rng.randint(0, 15)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(rest_len))
    return start + rest

def assemble_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a mix of formulas, captions, and defined names; each on its own line
    lines = []

    # Prioritize single-cell formulas used by all 3 chart_* stubs
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        lines.append(make_single_cell_formula(rng))

    # Add plausible captions
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 12)):
        lines.append(make_caption(rng))

    # Add defined names used by workbook_define_name stub
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        nm = make_defined_name(rng)
        # Also pair with a formula to reflect stub usage pattern
        lines.append(nm)

    # Add some explicitly quoted sheet formulas and absolute refs near small rows/cols
    for col in (1, 2, 26):
        row = rng.randint(1, 50)
        col_str = excel_col(col)
        sheet = "'Sales Q1'"
        lines.append(f"={sheet}!${col_str}${row}")

    payload = ("\n".join(lines)).encode('utf-8')
    return payload[:MAX_BUF]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_buffer(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Excel header/footer format strings
# Aim: produce valid, interesting strings using Excel control codes:
# - &L, &C, &R sections
# - Font: &"Font,Style"
# - Size: &N (number)
# - Bold/Italic/Underline/Subscript/Superscript: &B &I &U &Y &X (Excel uses &B, &I, &U, &E, &X in some contexts; libxlsxwriter supports &B, &I, &U, &S, &Y)
# - Page numbers: &P, &N
# - Date/Time: &D, &T
# - File/Sheet: &F, &A
# - Literal ampersand escaped as &&
# Constraints:
# - Printable ASCII only (32..126); ampersands doubled when literal text contains '&'.
# - Excel header/footer max 255 chars; fuzzer truncates input to ~250. We'll keep <= 240.

PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127) if chr(c) != '&')

LEFT = '&L'
CENTER = '&C'
RIGHT = '&R'

# Common tokens that exercise different code paths
TOKENS = [
    '&P',    # page number
    '&N',    # total pages
    '&D',    # date
    '&T',    # time
    '&F',    # file name
    '&A',    # sheet name
]

# Font names/styles to combine with &"Font,Style"
FONTS = [
    'Arial', 'Calibri', 'Times New Roman', 'Courier New', 'Tahoma', 'Verdana'
]
STYLES = ['Regular', 'Bold', 'Italic', 'Bold Italic']

# Some plain words to include
WORDS = [
    'Report', 'Summary', 'Confidential', 'Q1', 'FY2025', 'Draft', 'Final',
    'Revenue', 'Expenses', 'Chart', 'Data', 'Analysis'
]

# Valid formatting toggles supported by Excel headers/footers (subset)
FMT_TOGGLES = ['&B', '&I', '&U']


def esc_text(s: str) -> str:
    # Escape '&' by doubling
    return s.replace('&', '&&')


def rand_words(rng: random.Random, minw=1, maxw=4) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(minw, maxw)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            # random printable chunk
            k = rng.randint(3, 10)
            parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(k)))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(WORDS))
    return esc_text(' '.join(parts))


def font_spec(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # &"Font,Style"
    font = rng.choice(FONTS)
    style = rng.choice(STYLES)
    return f'&"{font},{style}"'


def size_spec(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # &N font size (integer 1..99). Use typical sizes 8..24, sometimes larger
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        n = rng.choice([8,9,10,11,12,14,16,18,20,24])
    else:
        n = rng.randint(6, 72)
    return f'&{n}'


def build_section(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Maybe start with a font spec and/or size
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(font_spec(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(size_spec(rng))
    # Toggle some formats
    for t in FMT_TOGGLES:
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(t)
    # Mix text and tokens
    m = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for i in range(m):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(rand_words(rng, 1, 3))
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(rng.choice(TOKENS))
        # Occasionally insert literal ampersand text to exercise escaping
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append(esc_text(' & '))
    # Trailing plain text sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rand_words(rng, 1, 2))
    sec = ' '.join(parts)
    # Ensure printable and limit length at section level too
    if len(sec) > 200:
        sec = sec[:200]
    return sec


def build_header_footer(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose L/C/R sections. At least one must exist; include 1-3 sections.
    sections = []
    order = [LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT]
    rng.shuffle(order)
    count = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for tag in order[:count]:
        sec = build_section(rng)
        sections.append(tag + sec)
    s = ''.join(sections)
    # Ensure not empty
    if not s:
        s = '&C' + rand_words(rng, 1, 2)
    # Constrain total length <= 240 to be comfortably within 255 after wrappers
    if len(s) > 240:
        s = s[:240]
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly decide header or footer flavor variety (same format works for both)
    s = build_header_footer(rng)
    # The fuzz stubs may further sanitize and double '&' as needed; we already ensure validity.
    # Return as UTF-8 bytes
    return s.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: alphanumeric string (letters and digits only)
# Fuzzer stubs consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - file extension key [a-z0-9]{1,8}
# - MIME type components (letters/digits/-.+ filtered, but we only provide alnum)
# - workbook/worksheet VBA names and defined names (letters/digits/_ allowed); we provide alnum and insert underscores sometimes.
# They also read two unsigned ints for producing a cell reference; we won’t embed those via FUZZ_PARAM_STR, so we focus on
# supplying strings that the harness sanitizes into valid values and exercise different code paths.
#
# Buffer layout: a series of NUL-terminated alphanumeric strings concatenated.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the harness typically pulls the next string chunk; by providing multiple interesting strings we can
# exercise different branches. Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
LOWER_NUM = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits


def _rand_alnum(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_lower_num(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(LOWER_NUM) for _ in range(n))


def _mime_like_pair(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce two alphanumeric tokens to be split by the harness into type/subtype by insertion of '/'
    a = _rand_lower_num(rng, 3, 8)
    b = _rand_lower_num(rng, 3, 12)
    return a + b


def _vba_name_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Start with a letter, then letters/digits; optionally include underscores inside (still alphanumeric required, but
    # underscore is allowed by consumers; however our type forbids punctuation. We can emulate underscores by providing
    # multiple names; harness accepts pure alnum too).
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 18)))
    return first + rest


def _defined_name_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Excel defined names allow letters, digits, underscore; provide alphanumeric which is valid enough after sanitization.
    return _vba_name_like(rng)


def _ext_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Lowercase/digits, length 1..8
    return _rand_lower_num(rng, 1, 8)


def _interesting_ext_keys() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "bin",    # common fallback in stub
        "xml",
        "rels",
        "png",
        "jpeg",
        "gif",
        "bmp",
        "vba",
    ]


def _interesting_mime_roots() -> List[str]:
    # Without '/', harness will insert slash mid-string
    return [
        "applicationoctetstream",    # becomes application/octetstream
        "textplain",                 # becomes text/plain
        "imagepng",                  # becomes image/png
        "imagejpeg",
        "applicationvndopenxmlformats",  # long
    ]


def _serialize_strings(chunks: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated ASCII chunks
    return b"".join(s.encode('ascii', 'ignore') + b"\x00" for s in chunks)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[str] = []

    # 1) Provide several extension keys for lxw_ct_add_default
    keys = _interesting_ext_keys()
    rng.shuffle(keys)
    # Add some random keys too
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        keys.append(_ext_key(rng))
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    ext_chunks = []
    for k in keys:
        if k not in seen and 1 <= len(k) <= 8:
            seen.add(k)
            ext_chunks.append(k)
    chunks.extend(ext_chunks)

    # 2) Provide MIME-like alnum strings that the stub will sanitize and insert '/'
    mime_roots = _interesting_mime_roots()
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        mime_roots.append(_mime_like_pair(rng))
    # Limit size and add
    chunks.extend(mime_roots[:rng.randint(5, 9)])

    # 3) Workbook defined names and VBA names
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        chunks.append(_defined_name_like(rng))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        chunks.append(_vba_name_like(rng))

    # 4) Worksheet VBA names
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        chunks.append(_vba_name_like(rng))

    # Ensure we have at least a couple of very short and very long alnum strings
    chunks.append(_rand_alnum(rng, 1, 2))
    chunks.append(_rand_alnum(rng, 15, 20))

    buf = _serialize_strings(chunks)
    # Trim to 4096 bytes if necessary, but keep last byte as NUL to avoid truncating a string mid-way without terminator
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4095] + b"\x00"
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: MIME type string (type/subtype) and path-like part names and extensions.
# Fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR to obtain:
#  - file extension key (1..8 chars, [a-z0-9])
#  - MIME type strings like type/subtype
#  - part names that should look like '/xl/...' paths
# This generator will pack several newline-separated strings that the harness can
# pull sequentially from FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls to yield valid inputs.

# Strategy:
#  - Produce a small corpus line-set mixing realistic extensions, part names, and MIME types.
#  - Ensure multiple alternatives per call by concatenating several candidates.
#  - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#  - Seeded randomness.

COMMON_EXTS = [
    "xml", "rels", "png", "jpeg", "jpg", "gif", "bmp", "bin", "xlsx",
    "vml", "svg", "json", "txt"
]

# Valid ASCII for stubs: lowercase letters, digits, and some punctuation for MIME types
_LOWER = string.ascii_lowercase
_DIGITS = string.digits

PRIMARY_TYPES = [
    "application", "image", "text", "audio", "video", "font"
]
SUBTYPES = {
    "application": [
        "xml", "zip", "json", "octet-stream", "vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
        "vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml", "pdf", "x-msdownload"
    ],
    "image": ["png", "jpeg", "gif", "bmp", "svg+xml", "webp"],
    "text": ["plain", "csv", "xml", "html", "css", "javascript"],
    "audio": ["mpeg", "wav", "ogg"],
    "video": ["mp4", "mpeg", "ogg"],
    "font": ["woff", "woff2", "ttf"]
}

# Typical part names used by libxlsxwriter
PART_NAMES = [
    "/[Content_Types].xml",
    "/_rels/.rels",
    "/xl/workbook.xml",
    "/xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels",
    "/xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml",
    "/xl/worksheets/sheet2.xml",
    "/xl/drawings/drawing1.xml",
    "/xl/charts/chart1.xml",
    "/xl/theme/theme1.xml",
    "/docProps/core.xml",
    "/docProps/app.xml",
    "/xl/media/image1.png",
]

# Additional plausible part names builder
def random_part_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a path like '/xl/some_dir/name.ext' with allowed characters
    bases = ["xl", "_rels", "docProps", "xl/worksheets", "xl/drawings", "xl/charts", "xl/media"]
    base = rng.choice(bases)
    leaf_name = ''.join(rng.choices(_LOWER + _DIGITS + "_-", k=rng.randint(5, 12)))
    ext = rng.choice(COMMON_EXTS)
    # Avoid double slashes if base already contains '/'
    if not base.startswith("/"):
        base = "/" + base
    if not base.endswith("/"):
        base = base + "/"
    return f"{base}{leaf_name}.{ext}"

# MIME type generator constrained to allowed characters in the stub
def random_mime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    typ = rng.choice(PRIMARY_TYPES)
    sub = rng.choice(SUBTYPES.get(typ, ["octet-stream"]))
    # Sanitize to allowed chars [a-z0-9-+./]
    def sanitize(s: str) -> str:
        allowed = set(_LOWER + _DIGITS + "-+./")
        return ''.join(ch for ch in s.lower() if ch in allowed)
    return f"{sanitize(typ)}/{sanitize(sub)}"

# Extension key generator (1..8 lowercase alnum)
def random_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        ext = rng.choice(COMMON_EXTS)
    else:
        ext = ''.join(rng.choices(_LOWER + _DIGITS, k=rng.randint(1, 8)))
    # Strip leading dots if any (though we don't add them) and limit length to 8
    return ext.strip('.').lower()[:8] or "bin"

# Build a corpus of lines that the fuzzer will consume via FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls in order.
# The stubs fetch, per operation:
#  - add_default: ext, mime
#  - add_override: part_name, mime
# We'll interleave multiple combos to exercise different paths.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    lines: List[str] = []

    # Seed with a few canonical pairs
    for _ in range(3):
        lines.append(random_ext(rng))
        lines.append(random_mime(rng))
        lines.append(random_part_name(rng))
        lines.append(random_mime(rng))

    # Add some well-known Excel-specific combos
    lines.extend([
        "xml", "application/xml",
        "/xl/workbook.xml", "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml",
        "/xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels", "application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml",
        "/[Content_Types].xml", "application/xml",
        "rels", "application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml",
        "png", "image/png",
    ])

    # More randomized combos to diversify
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        lines.append(random_ext(rng))
        lines.append(random_mime(rng))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 10)):
        lines.append(random_part_name(rng))
        lines.append(random_mime(rng))

    # Ensure lines are safe and within size; trim if needed
    blob = "\n".join(lines)
    b = blob.encode("utf-8")
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
        # Ensure we don't cut mid-line: trim back to last newline
        nl = b.rfind(b"\n")
        if nl != -1:
            b = b[:nl]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid, interesting path-like strings and MIME/type/URI-like
# strings tailored for the provided fuzzer stubs. The fuzzing framework will feed
# this single buffer to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls in sequence, so we concatenate several
# candidate strings separated by NULs. Each call to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() should then get
# the next segment.
#
# Target stubs expect:
# - OPC-like part names (path-like, possibly starting with '/').
# - MIME types like application/xml.
# - Worksheet part names tail to be combined with worksheets/<tail>N.xml by stub.
# - Relationship Type and Target strings (usually URI and path/part targets).
# - Optional TargetMode values are handled inside the stub.
#
# We therefore emit a sequence covering:
# 1) A fully qualified part name starting with '/'.
# 2) A relative part name (no leading '/').
# 3) Several worksheet tails with safe chars.
# 4) Valid MIME types and common OPC relationship Type URIs.
# 5) Relationship targets: relative parts, absolute part names, and external URLs.
# 6) Edge-y but valid names with dots, dashes, underscores, and nested folders.
#
# The buffer is <= 4096 bytes and contains only visible safe characters and NULs.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-."
PATH_SEP = "/"

MIME_TYPES = [
    "application/xml",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.worksheet+xml",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.theme+xml",
    "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.styles+xml",
]

# Common Relationship Type URIs from OPC/XLSX
REL_TYPE_URIS = [
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/officeDocument",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/worksheet",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/styles",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/theme",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/sharedStrings",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships/metadata/core-properties",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships/metadata/thumbnail",
    "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/chart",
]

EXTERNAL_URLS = [
    "http://example.com/",
    "https://example.com/data.xml",
    "https://contoso.example/path/file.bin",
]

# Useful path prefixes used in XLSX packages
PREFIXES = [
    "/xl/worksheets/",
    "xl/worksheets/",
    "/xl/",
    "xl/",
    "/docProps/",
    "docProps/",
    "/_rels/",
    "_rels/",
]

WORKSHEET_TAILS = [
    "sheet",
    "data",
    "Sheet",
    "ws_",
    "s-",
]

FOLDERS = [
    "charts",
    "drawings",
    "printerSettings",
    "tables",
    "embeddings",
]

FILENAMES = [
    "workbook.xml",
    "sharedStrings.xml",
    "styles.xml",
    "theme1.xml",
    "calcChain.xml",
]


def rand_id(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=10) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def make_part_path(rng: random.Random, absolute: bool = True) -> str:
    # Compose paths like /xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml or xl/charts/chartA.xml
    parts: List[str] = []
    # choose a base prefix
    base = rng.choice(PREFIXES)
    if absolute:
        if not base.startswith("/"):
            base = "/" + base
    else:
        base = base.lstrip("/")
    parts.append(base)

    # optionally add a folder
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(rng.choice(FOLDERS) + "/")

    # name stem
    stem = rng.choice([rng.choice(WORKSHEET_TAILS), rand_id(rng, 3, 8)])
    # optional numeric suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        stem += str(rng.randint(1, 999))
    # extension
    ext = rng.choice([".xml", ".bin", ".xml.rels"]) if rng.random() < 0.3 else ".xml"

    parts.append(stem + ext)

    # Join ensuring we don't end up with double slashes beyond the intentional ones in base
    path = "".join(parts)
    # sanitize accidental double slashes except leading //xl
    while "//" in path:
        path = path.replace("//", "/")
    # ensure at least one slash for relative when requested
    if not absolute and path.startswith("/"):
        path = path[1:]
    return path


def make_worksheet_tail(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # The stub appends worksheets/<tail>N.xml; supply a safe short tail
    base = rng.choice(WORKSHEET_TAILS)
    # insert some safe chars variety
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base += rand_id(rng, 1, 4)
    # keep within ~20 chars as stub truncates
    return base[:20]


def make_target(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    pick = rng.random()
    if pick < 0.5:
        return make_part_path(rng, absolute=False)
    elif pick < 0.8:
        return make_part_path(rng, absolute=True)
    else:
        return rng.choice(EXTERNAL_URLS)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    segments: List[str] = []

    # For lxw_ct_add_override: name then MIME
    segments.append(make_part_path(rng, absolute=rng.random() < 0.7))
    segments.append(rng.choice(MIME_TYPES))

    # For lxw_ct_add_worksheet_name: a tail base to be combined in stub
    segments.append(make_worksheet_tail(rng))

    # For relationships APIs we will need multiple Type/Target pairs; provide a pool
    # Document relationship
    segments.append(rng.choice(REL_TYPE_URIS))
    segments.append(make_target(rng))

    # Package relationship
    segments.append(rng.choice(REL_TYPE_URIS))
    segments.append(make_target(rng))

    # MS package relationship (can reuse same URIs or others)
    segments.append(rng.choice(REL_TYPE_URIS))
    segments.append(make_target(rng))

    # Worksheet relationship (Type, Target). Mode is chosen inside stub.
    segments.append(rng.choice(REL_TYPE_URIS))
    segments.append(make_target(rng))

    # Additional alternates to enrich subsequent FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls if any
    # Extra MIME types and paths
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        segments.append(make_part_path(rng, absolute=rng.random() < 0.5))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        segments.append(rng.choice(MIME_TYPES))

    # Ensure reasonable total size
    joined = b"\x00".join(s.encode('utf-8') for s in segments)
    return joined[:4096]
